extracted.intended_audience: individuals or organizations submitting citizen petitions to the FDA (including non-U.S. persons); counsel and regulatory affairs professionals preparing FDA petitions
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and mandatory requirements for preparing, formatting, filing, supplementing, and litigating citizen petitions submitted to the Food and Drug Administration under 21 CFR 10.30. Covers procedural timelines, docketing, required petition contents, and administrative-record rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: This section applies to any petition submitted by a person (including a person who is not a citizen of the United States) except to the extent that other sections of this chapter apply different requirements to a particular matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: General submission compliance (§10.20 and §10.31)
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition (including any attachments) must be submitted in accordance with §10.20 and, if applicable, §10.31. The certification requirement in this section does not apply to petitions subject to the certification requirement of §10.31.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure compliance with §10.20 (general submission requirements) and check whether §10.31 applies (verification/certification rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods of submission (electronic and non-electronic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions may be electronically submitted through http://www.regulations.gov (Docket No. FDA 2013-S-0610). If not electronically submitted, deliver to Dockets Management Staff address. It is only necessary to submit one copy electronically; non-electronic confidential petitions require two copies (original and redacted); otherwise only one copy is necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the specified docket number and address exactly; use electronic filing where possible; for confidential materials submit original + redacted when filing by mail/delivery service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required petition format (overall template)
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition must follow the Citizen Petition format: include Date; a statement that the undersigned submits the petition under relevant statutory sections and requests the Commissioner to issue, amend, or revoke a regulation or order or to take/refrain from other administrative action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the provided template headings and structure to avoid procedural defects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Action Requested content
rubrics_metrics.description: If the petition requests the Commissioner to issue, amend, or revoke a regulation, provide the exact wording of the existing regulation (if any) and the proposed regulation or amendment requested. If requesting issuance/amendment/revocation of an order, provide a copy of the exact wording of the citation to the existing order (if any) and the exact wording requested for the proposed order. If requesting other administrative action, specify the specific action or relief requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide verbatim text comparisons (existing and proposed) or precise citations so agency can identify the requested textual change or action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of Grounds (full factual and legal statement)
rubrics_metrics.description: A full statement, in a well-organized format, of the factual and legal grounds on which the petitioner relies, including all relevant information and views on which the petitioner relies, as well as representative information known to the petitioner which is unfavorable to the petitioner's position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be comprehensive and transparent: include supportive evidence and disclose unfavorable representative information; organize grounds clearly to facilitate agency review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental Impact requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Include either (A) a claim for categorical exclusion under §§25.30–25.34 of this chapter or (B) an environmental assessment under §25.40 of this chapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State explicitly whether you claim a categorical exclusion and cite the applicable §25.3x provision, or attach a full environmental assessment per §25.40 when required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economic Impact information (when requested)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a statement of the effect of the requested action on: (1) cost (and price) increases to industry, government, and consumers; (2) productivity of wage earners, businesses, or government; (3) competition; (4) supplies of important materials, products, or services; (5) employment; and (6) energy supply or demand — but only when requested by the Commissioner following review of the petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not include detailed economic analysis unless requested; be prepared to supply impact data addressing the listed aspects if the FDA asks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification statement
rubrics_metrics.description: The undersigned certifies, that, to the best knowledge and belief of the undersigned, this petition includes all information and views on which the petition relies, and that it includes representative data and information known to the petitioner which are unfavorable to the petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a signed certification with contact information (signature, name, mailing address, telephone). Note §10.31 may impose different verification requirements for certain petitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing and docketing procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition that appears to meet format and submission requirements will be filed by Dockets Management Staff, stamped with the date of filing, and assigned a unique docket number which identifies the docket file for all submissions relating to the petition. Subsequent submissions must refer to the assigned docket number. Related petitions may be filed together and given the same docket number. Dockets Management Staff will promptly notify the petitioner of filing and assigned docket number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference the docket number on all subsequent submissions and communications; combine related petitions when appropriate to share a single docket.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public comment on petition
rubrics_metrics.description: An interested person may submit comments to Dockets Management Staff on a filed petition; such comments become part of the docket file, must specify the petition docket number, and include verification under §10.31 if applicable. Comments may support or oppose the petition in whole or in part. A request for alternative or different administrative action must be submitted as a separate petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third-party commenters should include verification when required; alternative relief requests should be filed as distinct petitions rather than as comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioner's consideration factors when ruling
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner shall rule on each filed petition taking into consideration: (i) available agency resources for the category of subject matter, (ii) the priority assigned to the petition considering both the category of subject matter involved and the overall work of the agency, and (iii) time requirements established by statute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitioners should be aware that agency resource constraints and competing priorities affect timing and disposition; statutory time requirements may control in some cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response timelines and exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as provided in paragraphs (e)(4) and (5), the Commissioner shall furnish a response within 180 days of receipt. The Commissioner shall furnish a response within 90 days for petitions filed under section 505(j)(2)(C) of the Act. The Commissioner intends to furnish a response within 150 days for petitions subject to section 505(q) of the Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect a general 180-day response target but special statutory provisions can shorten the response period for certain types of petitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Possible agency responses
rubrics_metrics.description: The response will either: (i) Approve the petition, in which case the Commissioner shall concurrently take appropriate action (e.g., publication of a Federal Register notice) implementing the approval; (ii) Deny the petition; (iii) Dismiss the petition if changes in law, facts, or circumstances have rendered it moot; or (iv) Provide a tentative response explaining delay or additional information needed, possibly indicating the likely ultimate agency response and when a final response may be furnished.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared for full approval, denial, dismissal as moot, or a tentative response that may foreshadow the final decision and provide timing expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency authority over relief and dismissal
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner may grant or deny such a petition, in whole or in part, and may grant such other relief or take other action as the petition warrants. If changes in law, facts, or circumstances render the petition moot, the Commissioner may dismiss the petition. The petitioner is to be notified of the decision; the decision will be placed in the public docket file and may also be published in the Federal Register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relief may be tailored; expect public availability of decisions and potential Federal Register notices implementing approvals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of rulemaking procedures when regulation requested
rubrics_metrics.description: If a petition requests the Commissioner to issue, amend, or revoke a regulation, §10.40 or §10.50 also apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions seeking regulatory text changes will trigger additional rulemaking procedures and requirements under the cited sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementing, amending, or withdrawing a petition
rubrics_metrics.description: A petitioner may supplement, amend, or withdraw a petition without Agency approval and without prejudice to resubmission at any time until the Commissioner rules on the petition, unless the petition has been referred for a hearing under parts 12, 13, 14, or 15. After a ruling or referral, a petition may be supplemented, amended, or withdrawn only with the approval of the Commissioner. The Commissioner may approve withdrawal, with or without prejudice against resubmission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior to ruling, petitioners may freely revise or withdraw; after referral to hearing or after a ruling, obtain Commissioner approval to make changes or withdraw.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review procedures the Commissioner may use
rubrics_metrics.description: In reviewing a petition, the Commissioner may use: (1) conferences, meetings, discussions, and correspondence under §10.65; (2) a hearing under parts 12–16; (3) a Federal Register notice requesting information and views; (4) a proposal to issue, amend, or revoke a regulation, in accordance with §10.40 or §12.20; (5) any other specific public procedure established in this chapter and expressly applicable to the matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitioners should be prepared for a range of agency procedures including public notice-and-comment, hearings, or meetings; follow applicable procedural cross-references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composition of the administrative record
rubrics_metrics.description: The record consists of: (1) the petition and all information on which it relies filed by Dockets Management Staff; (2) all comments received on the petition; (3) if petition resulted in a proposal to issue/amend/revoke a regulation, documents specified in §10.40(g); (4) the record from optional procedures (transcripts, minutes, reports, Federal Register notices, except transcripts of closed portions of public advisory committee meetings); (5) the Commissioner's decision and supporting information filed with Dockets Management Staff; (6) all documents filed under §10.65(h); (7) if a petition for reconsideration or for a stay is filed under paragraph (j), the administrative record specified in §10.33(k) or §10.35(h).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure all supporting materials are filed timely because they become part of the exclusive administrative record supporting the decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusivity of the administrative record and post-decision submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: The administrative record specified is the exclusive record for the Commissioner's decision. The record closes on the date of the Commissioner's decision unless some other date is specified. Thereafter any interested person may submit a petition for reconsideration under §10.33 or a petition for stay of action under §10.35. A person who wishes to rely upon information or views not included in the administrative record shall submit them to the Commissioner with a new petition to modify the decision in accordance with this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume late-submitted materials will be considered in the original decision; submit new petitions if relying on information not in the closed record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusions and routine correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: This section does not apply to referral of a matter to a United States attorney for court enforcement action and related correspondence, or to requests, suggestions, and recommendations made informally in routine correspondence received by FDA. Routine correspondence does not constitute a petition unless it purports to meet the requirements of this section. Action on routine correspondence does not constitute final administrative action subject to judicial review under §10.45.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal petition requirements are distinct from routine or enforcement-referral communications; do not treat informal communications as petitions unless they explicitly comply with §10.30 requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dockets Management Staff tracking obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Dockets Management Staff will maintain a chronological list of each petition filed under this section and §10.85 showing: (1) docket number; (2) date the petition was filed; (3) name of the petitioner; (4) subject matter involved; and (5) disposition of the petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitioners can expect public tracking of filing date, petitioner identity, subject, and disposition via Dockets Management Staff listings.
